title.narrative: Sierra Leone and Liberia Disaster Risk Reduction

description.narrative:
Sierra Leone and Liberia are facing series of disasters, both natural and human-induced. There is a probability for more disasters in future as most people in both countries are living in vulnerable conditions and are exposed to lots of hazards. Climate change is also impacting greatly in these two countries which increases both the incidence and severity of disasters.
Caritas partners in Sierra Leone and Liberia have been responding to disasters as they are engaged in poverty reduction and sustainable development programmes. They however, do not have an in built focus on DRR. In Sierra Leone, there is an established Office of National Security with a disaster management department mandated to deal with disasters. A policy has been formulated that is awaiting enactment by parliament. Also in Liberia, the government and it partners have developed an integrated contingency plan which is part of the National Action Plan for Disaster Risk Reduction. However this document focuses solely on immediate and urgent life saving needs of people affected by disasters.
This project aims at fully integrating DRR into the development programmes implemented by partners in order to add value to their humanitarian and development work and making the latter more sustainable. The DRR project will commence with capacity building of partners in the form of training that will be organized in March 2009. This PSGA is developed to facilitate the training of all partners and further proceed with the DRR concept.
